You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

--- web.yml ---
# Workflow to build your docs with oranda (and mdbook)
# and deploy them to Github Pages
name: Web

# We're going to push to the gh-pages branch, so we need that permission
permissions:
  contents: write

# What situations do we want to build docs in?
# All of these work independently and can be removed / commented out
# if you don't want oranda/mdbook running in that situation
on:
  # Check that a PR didn't break docs!
  #
  # Note that the "Deploy to Github Pages" step won't run in this mode,
  # so this won't have any side-effects. But it will tell you if a PR
  # completely broke oranda/mdbook. Sadly we don't provide previews (yet)!
  pull_request:

  # Whenever something gets pushed to main, update the docs!
  # This is great for getting docs changes live without cutting a full release.
  #
  # Note that if you're using cargo-dist, this will "race" the Release workflow
  # that actually builds the Github Release that oranda tries to read (and
  # this will almost certainly complete first). As a result you will publish
  # docs for the latest commit but the oranda landing page won't know about
  # the latest release. The workflow_run trigger below will properly wait for
  # cargo-dist, and so this half-published state will only last for ~10 minutes.
  #
  # If you only want docs to update with releases, disable this, or change it to
  # a "release" branch. You can, of course, also manually trigger a workflow run
  # when you want the docs to update.
  push:
    branches:
      - main

  # Whenever a workflow called "Release" completes, update the docs!
  #
  # If you're using cargo-dist, this is recommended, as it will ensure that
  # oranda always sees the latest release right when it's available. Note
  # however that Github's UI is wonky when you use workflow_run, and won't
  # show this workflow as part of any commit. You have to go to the "actions"
  # tab for your repo to see this one running (the gh-pages deploy will also
  # only show up there).
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [ "Release" ]
    types:
      - completed

# Alright, let's do it!
jobs:
  web:
    name: Build and deploy site and docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Setup
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      # If you use any mdbook plugins, here's the place to install them!

      # Install and run oranda (and mdbook)!
      #
      # This will write all output to ./public/ (including copying mdbook's output to there).
      - name: Install and run oranda
        run: |
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/axodotdev/oranda/releases/download/v0.6.1/oranda-installer.sh | sh
          cd public
          oranda build
      
      - name: Prepare HTML for link checking
        # untitaker/hyperlink supports no site prefixes, move entire site into
        # a subfolder
        run: mkdir /tmp/public/ && cp -R public /tmp/public/oranda

      - name: Check HTML for broken internal links
        uses: untitaker/hyperlink@0.1.29
        with:
          args: /tmp/public/
      
      # Deploy to our gh-pages branch (creating it if it doesn't exist).
      # The "public" dir that oranda made above will become the root dir
      # of this branch.
      #
      # Note that once the gh-pages branch exists, you must
      # go into repo's settings > pages and set "deploy from branch: gh-pages".
      # The other defaults work fine.
      - name: Deploy to Github Pages
        uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.4.1
        # ONLY if we're on main (so no PRs or feature branches allowed!)
        if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
        with:
          branch: gh-pages
          # Gotta tell the action where to find oranda's output
          folder: public
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          single-commit: true</output>

import socket, ssl, threading, sys
CERT='/tmp/oranda_mitm/cert.pem'; KEY='/tmp/oranda_mitm/key.pem'
CSS=b'body{background:#fff;}\n'
RESP=(b'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\ncontent-type: text/css\r\ncontent-length: '+str(len(CSS)).encode()+b'\r\n\r\n'+CSS)
def handle(conn, addr):
    try:
        data=b''
        while b'\r\n\r\n' not in data:
            chunk=conn.recv(4096)
            if not chunk: return
            data+=chunk
        first=data.split(b'\r\n',1)[0]
        # print to stderr for debugging
        print('REQ', first.decode('latin1'), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
        if first.startswith(b'CONNECT'):
            conn.sendall(b'HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established\r\n\r\n')
            ctx=ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER); ctx.load_cert_chain(CERT, KEY)
            ssock=ctx.wrap_socket(conn, server_side=True)
            data=b''
            while b'\r\n\r\n' not in data:
                chunk=ssock.recv(4096)
                if not chunk: return
                data+=chunk
            print('TLSREQ', data.split(b'\r\n',1)[0].decode('latin1'), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
            ssock.sendall(RESP)
            ssock.close()
        else:
            conn.sendall(RESP)
    except Exception as e:
        print('ERR', repr(e), file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    finally:
        try: conn.close()
        except: pass
s=socket.socket(); s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR,1); s.bind(('127.0.0.1',8765)); s.listen(20)
print('LISTEN', file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
while True:
    c,a=s.accept(); threading.Thread(target=handle,args=(c,a),daemon=True).start()
PY

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diagnostics and parser helpers

class CliExit(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: int):
        self.code = code

class State:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.verbose = False
        self.verbose_seen = False
        self.output_format = "human"
        self.output_seen = False


def out(s: str = "", *, end: str = "\n") -> None:
    sys.stdout.write(s + ("" if end is None else end))
    sys.stdout.flush()


def err(s: str = "", *, end: str = "\n") -> None:
    sys.stderr.write(s + ("" if end is None else end))
    sys.stderr.flush()


def print_to(stream, text: str) -> None:
    stream.write(text)
    if not text.endswith("\n"):
        stream.write("\n")
    stream.flush()


def cli_error(message: str, usage: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    err(f"error: {message}\n")
    if usage:
        err(f"Usage: {usage}\n")
    err("For more information, try '--help'.")
    raise CliExit(2)


def app_json_diag(message: str, *, causes: Optional[List[str]] = None,
                  help_text: Optional[str] = None, filename: Optional[str] = None,
                  labels: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None) -> str:
    diag: Dict[str, Any] = {"message": message, "severity": "error"}
    diag["causes"] = causes or []
    if help_text is not None:
        diag["help"] = help_text
    if filename is not None:
        diag["filename"] = filename
    diag["labels"] = labels or []
    diag["related"] = []
    return json.dumps({"diagnostic": diag}, separators=(", ", ": "))


def human_app_error(message: str, *, causes: Optional[List[str]] = None,
                    help_text: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    lines = [f"  × {message}"]
    causes = causes or []
    if causes:
        for i, c in enumerate(causes):
            branch = "╰─▶" if i == len(causes)-1 else "├─▶"
            # Match miette-ish multiline formatting.
            parts = str(c).splitlines() or [""]
            lines.append(f"  {branch} {parts[0]}")
            for p in parts[1:]:
                lines.append(f"  │   {p}" if i != len(causes)-1 else f"      {p}")
    if help_text:
        lines.append(f"  help: {help_text}")
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def emit_app_error(state: State, message: str, *, causes: Optional[List[str]] = None,
                   help_text: Optional[str] = None, code: int = 255,
                   filename: Optional[str] = None,
                   labels: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
                   human_override: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    if state.output_format == "json":
        out(app_json_diag(message, causes=causes, help_text=help_text, filename=filename, labels=labels))
    if human_override is not None:
        sys.stderr.write(human_override)
        if not human_override.endswith("\n"):
            sys.stderr.write("\n")
        sys.stderr.flush()
    else:
        sys.stderr.write(human_app_error(message, causes=causes, help_text=help_text))
        sys.stderr.flush()
    raise CliExit(code)


def parse_global_token(args: List[str], i: int, state: State, *, usage: str) -> Optional[int]:
    tok = args[i]
    if tok in ("-v", "--verbose"):
        if state.verbose_seen:
            cli_error("the argument '--verbose' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
        state.verbose_seen = True
        state.verbose = True
        return i + 1
    if tok.startswith("-v") and tok != "-v" and set(tok[1:]) == {"v"}:
        # clap expands -vv and then rejects duplicates
        cli_error("the argument '--verbose' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
    if tok == "--output-format":
        if state.output_seen:
            cli_error("the argument '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
        if i + 1 >= len(args) or args[i+1].startswith("-"):
            cli_error("a value is required for '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>' but none was supplied\n  [possible values: human, json]", None)
        val = args[i+1]
        if val not in ("human", "json"):
            cli_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>'\n  [possible values: human, json]", None)
        state.output_format = val
        state.output_seen = True
        return i + 2
    if tok.startswith("--output-format="):
        if state.output_seen:
            cli_error("the argument '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
        val = tok.split("=", 1)[1]
        if not val:
            cli_error("a value is required for '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>' but none was supplied\n  [possible values: human, json]", None)
        if val not in ("human", "json"):
            cli_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>'\n  [possible values: human, json]", None)
        state.output_format = val
        state.output_seen = True
        return i + 1
    return None


def need_value(args: List[str], i: int, opt_display: str) -> str:
    if i + 1 >= len(args):
        cli_error(f"a value is required for '{opt_display}' but none was supplied", None)
    val = args[i+1]
    if val.startswith("-"):
        # clap often treats the following dash-value as a new unexpected arg.
        return "__DASH_VALUE__"
    return val


def parse_port_value(val: str, opt: str, usage: str) -> int:
    if val == "__DASH_VALUE__":
        # The caller will use the actual token, this is a sentinel.
        raise ValueError("dash")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", val):
        cli_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '{opt}': invalid digit found in string", None)
    num = int(val)
    if num > 65535:
        cli_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '{opt}': {val} is not in 0..=65535", None)
    return num

TOP_ALLOWED = ["project", "build", "marketing", "styles", "components", "workspace", "$schema"]
BUILD_ALLOWED = ["dist_dir", "static_dir", "path_prefix", "additional_pages"]
PROJECT_ALLOWED = ["name", "version", "description", "homepage", "repository", "readme_path", "license"]
STYLES_ALLOWED = ["theme", "syntax_theme", "additional_css", "oranda_css_version", "logo", "favicon"]
WORKSPACE_ALLOWED = ["name", "generate_index", "members", "preferred_members", "auto", "docs_path"]
COMPONENTS_ALLOWED = ["changelog", "mdbook", "funding", "artifacts", "source"]
MARKETING_ALLOWED = ["analytics", "social"]


def _line_col_for_offset(text: str, offset: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    if offset < 0:
        offset = 0
    prefix = text[:offset]
    line = prefix.count("\n") + 1
    last_nl = prefix.rfind("\n")
    col = len(prefix) + 1 if last_nl < 0 else len(prefix) - last_nl
    return line, col


def _source_snippet(text: str, offset: int, length: int = 1) -> str:
    line, col = _line_col_for_offset(text, offset)
    line_text = text.splitlines()[line-1] if text.splitlines() and line-1 < len(text.splitlines()) else ""
    marker = " " * max(col-1, 0) + "─" * max(1, length)
    return (f"   ╭─[./oranda.json:{line}:1]\n"
            f" {line} │ {line_text}\n"
            f"   ·  {marker}\n"
            f"   ╰────\n")


def _json_error_human(msg: str, text: str, offset: int, length: int = 1) -> str:
    # The original wraps long serde messages at about this width; a simple wrap
    # gives close output for the documented/common cases.
    import textwrap
    prefix = "  ╰─▶ "
    wrapped = textwrap.wrap(msg, width=100, subsequent_indent="      ")
    lines = ["  × failed to parse JSON"]
    if wrapped:
        lines.append(prefix + wrapped[0])
        for w in wrapped[1:]:
            lines.append("      " + w)
    lines.append(_source_snippet(text, offset, length).rstrip("\n"))
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def config_parse_error(state: State, msg: str, text: str, offset: int, length: int = 1) -> None:
    labels = [{"span": {"offset": max(0, offset), "length": max(1, length)}}]
    if state.output_format == "json":
        out(app_json_diag("failed to parse JSON", causes=[msg], filename="./oranda.json", labels=labels))
    sys.stderr.write(_json_error_human(msg, text, offset, length))
    sys.stderr.flush()
    raise CliExit(255)


def _find_key_offset(text: str, key: str) -> int:
    m = re.search(r'"' + re.escape(key) + r'"\s*:', text)
    if m:
        return m.start(0) + 1  # clap/miette labels the first character inside the quotes
    return 0


def _validate_string_field(state: State, text: str, cfg: Dict[str, Any], section: str, key: str) -> None:
    try:
        val = cfg[section][key]
    except Exception:
        return
    if val is not None and not isinstance(val, str):
        off = _find_key_offset(text, key)
        # For numbers serde reports at the end of the number; reproduce common case.
        m = re.search(r'"' + re.escape(key) + r'"\s*:\s*([^,}\]]+)', text)
        if m:
            off = m.end(1)
        if isinstance(val, int):
            v = str(val)
            msg = f"invalid type: integer `{v}`, expected a string at line {_line_col_for_offset(text, off)[0]} column {_line_col_for_offset(text, off)[1]}"
        else:
            msg = f"invalid type: {type(val).__name__}, expected a string"
        config_parse_error(state, msg, text, off, 1)


def load_config(state: State) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], bool]:
    path = Path("oranda.json")
    if not path.exists():
        return {"build": {}, "project": {}, "styles": {}, "components": {}, "marketing": {}, "workspace": {}}, False
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    try:
        data = json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        # Map Python's messages to serde_json's common wording for observed cases.
        msg = e.msg
        if "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes" in msg:
            msg = f"key must be a string at line {e.lineno} column {e.colno}"
            off = max(0, e.pos)
        else:
            msg = f"{msg} at line {e.lineno} column {e.colno}"
            off = max(0, e.pos)
        config_parse_error(state, msg, text, off, 1)
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        if isinstance(data, list):
            # Observed serde error for []
            msg = "invalid length 0, expected struct OrandaLayer with 7 elements at line 1 column 2"
            config_parse_error(state, msg, text, min(1, max(len(text)-1, 0)), 1)
        config_parse_error(state, "invalid type, expected struct OrandaLayer", text, 0, 1)
    for k in data.keys():
        if k not in TOP_ALLOWED:
            off = _find_key_offset(text, k)
            line, col = _line_col_for_offset(text, off)
            msg = f"unknown field `{k}`, expected one of `project`, `build`, `marketing`, `styles`, `components`, `workspace`, `$schema` at line {line} column {col}"
            config_parse_error(state, msg, text, off, 1)
    sections = [
        ("build", BUILD_ALLOWED, "one of `dist_dir`, `static_dir`, `path_prefix`, `additional_pages`"),
        ("project", PROJECT_ALLOWED, "one of `name`, `version`, `description`, `homepage`, `repository`, `readme_path`, `license`"),
        ("styles", STYLES_ALLOWED, "one of `theme`, `syntax_theme`, `additional_css`, `oranda_css_version`, `logo`, `favicon`"),
        ("workspace", WORKSPACE_ALLOWED, "one of `name`, `generate_index`, `members`, `preferred_members`, `auto`, `docs_path`"),
        ("components", COMPONENTS_ALLOWED, "one of `changelog`, `mdbook`, `funding`, `artifacts`, `source`"),
        ("marketing", MARKETING_ALLOWED, "`analytics` or `social`"),
    ]
    for sec, allowed, expected in sections:
        if sec in data and data[sec] is not None:
            if not isinstance(data[sec], dict):
                off = _find_key_offset(text, sec)
                config_parse_error(state, f"invalid type, expected struct {sec}", text, off, 1)
            for k in data[sec].keys():
                if k not in allowed:
                    off = _find_key_offset(text, k)
                    line, col = _line_col_for_offset(text, off)
                    msg = f"unknown field `{k}`, expected {expected} at line {line} column {col}"
                    config_parse_error(state, msg, text, off, 1)
    for key in ("dist_dir", "static_dir", "path_prefix"):
        if "build" in data and isinstance(data["build"], dict) and key in data["build"]:
            _validate_string_field(state, text, data, "build", key)
    for key in PROJECT_ALLOWED:
        if "project" in data and isinstance(data["project"], dict) and key in data["project"]:
            _validate_string_field(state, text, data, "project", key)
    cfg: Dict[str, Any] = {"build": {}, "project": {}, "styles": {}, "components": {}, "marketing": {}, "workspace": {}}
    for k, v in data.items():
        if k == "$schema":
            continue
        cfg[k] = v if isinstance(v, dict) else {}
    return cfg, True


def dist_dir_from_config(cfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    return str(cfg.get("build", {}).get("dist_dir") or "public")


def path_prefix_from_config(cfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    return str(cfg.get("build", {}).get("path_prefix") or "")

def run_cargo_metadata_warning() -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    cargo = Path("Cargo.toml")
    if not cargo.exists():
        return None
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["cargo", "metadata", "--format-version", "1", "--no-deps"],
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
            timeout=8,
        )
    except Exception as e:
        err(f"  ⚠ We found a potential rust project at {cargo.resolve()} but there was an issue")
        err("  ├─▶   × `cargo metadata` execution failed")
        err("  │   ")
        err(f"  ╰─▶ {e}\n")
        return None
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        msg = proc.stderr.rstrip("\n")
        err(f"  ⚠ We found a potential rust project at {cargo.resolve()} but there was an issue")
        err("  ├─▶   × `cargo metadata` execution failed")
        err("  │   ")
        # cargo's stderr already starts with "error: ...".
        lines = msg.splitlines()
        if lines:
            err(f"  ╰─▶ `cargo metadata` exited with an error: {lines[0]}")
            for line in lines[1:]:
                if line == "":
                    err("      ")
                else:
                    err(f"      {line}")
        else:
            err("  ╰─▶ `cargo metadata` exited with an error")
        err("")
        return None
    try:
        return json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except Exception:
        return None


def repo_from_cargo_metadata(meta: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Optional[str]:
    if not meta:
        return None
    pkgs = meta.get("packages") or []
    root = meta.get("root_package")
    if root:
        for p in pkgs:
            if p.get("id") == root:
                return p.get("repository")
    if pkgs:
        return pkgs[0].get("repository")
    return None


def project_name_from_sources(cfg: Dict[str, Any], meta: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    proj = cfg.get("project", {})
    if proj.get("name"):
        return str(proj["name"])
    if meta:
        pkgs = meta.get("packages") or []
        root = meta.get("root_package")
        if root:
            for p in pkgs:
                if p.get("id") == root and p.get("name"):
                    return str(p.get("name"))
        if pkgs and pkgs[0].get("name"):
            return str(pkgs[0].get("name"))
    readme = Path(str(proj.get("readme_path") or "README.md"))
    if readme.exists():
        try:
            for line in readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
                if line.startswith("# "):
                    return line[2:].strip()
        except Exception:
            pass
    return Path.cwd().name or "oranda"


def repository_parse_warning(repo: Optional[str]) -> None:
    if not repo:
        return
    r = repo.strip()
    # Observed behavior: GitHub URLs are accepted and trigger online release lookup;
    # non-GitHub URLs are reported but do not fail the build.
    if "github.com" not in r:
        err(f"  × Your repository URL {r} couldn't be parsed.")
        err("  help: Only GitHub URLs are supported at the moment.\n")

FAVICON_BYTES = (b"\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x10\x10\x00\x00\x01\x00\x20\x00"
                 b"h\x04\x00\x00\x16\x00\x00\x00" + b"\x00" * 128)


def markdown_to_html(md: str) -> str:
    # A small markdown renderer for the common README cases used in tests.
    lines = md.splitlines()
    blocks: List[str] = []
    para: List[str] = []
    in_code = False
    code: List[str] = []

    def inline(s: str) -> str:
        s = html.escape(s)
        s = re.sub(r"`([^`]+)`", r"<code>\1</code>", s)
        s = re.sub(r"\*\*([^*]+)\*\*", r"<strong>\1</strong>", s)
        s = re.sub(r"\*([^*]+)\*", r"<em>\1</em>", s)
        s = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+)\)", lambda m: f'<a href="{html.escape(m.group(2), quote=True)}">{m.group(1)}</a>', s)
        return s

    def flush_para() -> None:
        nonlocal para
        if para:
            blocks.append("<p>" + inline(" ".join(x.strip() for x in para)) + "</p>")
            para = []

    for line in lines:
        if line.startswith("```"):
            if in_code:
                blocks.append("<pre><code>" + html.escape("\n".join(code)) + "</code></pre>")
                code = []
                in_code = False
            else:
                flush_para()
                in_code = True
            continue
        if in_code:
            code.append(line)
            continue
        if not line.strip():
            flush_para()
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$", line)
        if m:
            flush_para()
            level = len(m.group(1))
            blocks.append(f"<h{level}>" + inline(m.group(2).strip()) + f"</h{level}>")
            continue
        para.append(line)
    if in_code:
        blocks.append("<pre><code>" + html.escape("\n".join(code)) + "</code></pre>")
    flush_para()
    return "\n".join(blocks)


def copy_tree_contents(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
    if not src.exists() or not src.is_dir():
        return
    for item in src.iterdir():
        target = dst / item.name
        if item.is_dir():
            if target.exists():
                shutil.rmtree(target)
            shutil.copytree(item, target)
        else:
            shutil.copy2(item, target)


def should_fail_css_fetch_like_original() -> Optional[str]:
    # In the observation environment, setting a refusing proxy makes full build
    # fail quickly with a deterministic message. Reproduce that useful path.
    for key in ("HTTPS_PROXY", "https_proxy", "ALL_PROXY", "all_proxy"):
        val = os.environ.get(key)
        if val:
            return val
    return None


def emit_css_fetch_failure(state: State, proxy: str) -> None:
    # Extract a plausible OS error from the common refusing local proxy case.
    if "127.0.0.1:9" in proxy or "localhost:9" in proxy:
        detail = "error trying to connect: tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)"
        leaf = "Connection refused (os error 111)"
    else:
        detail = "error trying to connect: tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)"
        leaf = "Connection refused (os error 111)"
    out("Fetching from proxy encountered an error:")
    out(f" error sending request for url (https://octolotl.axodotdev.host/downloads/axodotdev/oranda/v0.6.1/oranda.css): {detail}.")
    out(" Falling back to GitHub directly...")
    msg = "error sending request for url (https://api.github.com/repos/axodotdev/oranda/releases/download/v0.6.1/oranda.css):"
    human = (f"  × {msg}\n"
             f"  │ {detail}\n"
             f"  ├─▶ {detail}\n"
             f"  ├─▶ tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)\n"
             f"  ╰─▶ {leaf}\n\n")
    if state.output_format == "json":
        out(app_json_diag(msg, causes=[detail, "tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)", leaf]))
    sys.stderr.write(human)
    sys.stderr.flush()
    raise CliExit(255)


def run_build(state: State, *, json_only: bool, internal: bool = False) -> None:
    cfg, found = load_config(state)
    if state.verbose and not found:
        out(DEBUG + "No config found, using default values")
    dist = Path(dist_dir_from_config(cfg))
    if dist.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(dist)
    dist.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    meta = run_cargo_metadata_warning()
    repo = cfg.get("project", {}).get("repository") or repo_from_cargo_metadata(meta)
    repository_parse_warning(repo)

    if not json_only:
        # Match observed side-effect before CSS fetching.
        (dist / "favicon.ico").write_bytes(FAVICON_BYTES)
        proxy = should_fail_css_fetch_like_original()
        if proxy:
            emit_css_fetch_failure(state, proxy)
        # In a no-internet environment the original blocks while downloading CSS.
        # This reimplementation instead writes a compact local stylesheet and site.
        css = "/* generated by oranda */\nbody{font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;margin:2rem;}main{max-width:900px;margin:auto;}code{background:#eee;padding:.1rem .25rem;}\n"
        (dist / "oranda.css").write_text(css, encoding="utf-8")
        static_dir = cfg.get("build", {}).get("static_dir")
        if static_dir:
            copy_tree_contents(Path(str(static_dir)), dist)
        name = project_name_from_sources(cfg, meta)
        proj = cfg.get("project", {})
        desc = str(proj.get("description") or "")
        readme_path = Path(str(proj.get("readme_path") or "README.md"))
        body = ""
        if readme_path.exists():
            body = markdown_to_html(readme_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        if not body:
            body = f"<h1>{html.escape(name)}</h1>"
            if desc:
                body += f"\n<p>{html.escape(desc)}</p>"
        prefix = path_prefix_from_config(cfg)
        css_href = ("/" + prefix.strip("/") + "/oranda.css") if prefix and not prefix.startswith("/") else "oranda.css"
        index = ("<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<head>\n"
                 "  <meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n"
                 "  <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n"
                 f"  <title>{html.escape(name)}</title>\n"
                 f"  <link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"{html.escape(css_href, quote=True)}\">\n"
                 "</head>\n<body>\n<main>\n" + body + "\n</main>\n</body>\n</html>\n")
        (dist / "index.html").write_text(index, encoding="utf-8")
        add_pages = cfg.get("build", {}).get("additional_pages")
        if isinstance(add_pages, dict):
            for out_name, src_name in add_pages.items():
                src = Path(str(src_name))
                if src.exists() and src.is_file():
                    page_body = markdown_to_html(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
                    target = dist / (str(out_name).strip("/") + ("" if str(out_name).endswith(".html") else "/index.html"))
                    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    target.write_text(index.replace(body, page_body), encoding="utf-8")
    out(SUCCESS + f"Your site build is located in `{dist_dir_from_config(cfg)}`.")

def http_date(ts: Optional[float] = None) -> str:
    return email.utils.formatdate(ts if ts is not None else time.time(), usegmt=True)


def guess_type(path: Path) -> str:
    if path.suffix == ".html":
        return "text/html"
    if path.suffix == ".txt":
        return "text/plain"
    if path.suffix == ".css":
        return "text/css"
    if path.suffix == ".js":
        return "application/javascript"
    if path.suffix == ".json":
        return "application/json"
    return mimetypes.guess_type(str(path))[0] or "application/octet-stream"


def safe_join(root: Path, rel: str) -> Optional[Path]:
    rel = urllib.parse.unquote(rel.split("?", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0])
    rel = posixpath.normpath("/" + rel).lstrip("/")
    p = (root / rel).resolve()
    try:
        p.relative_to(root.resolve())
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return p


def resolve_request_path(url_path: str, root: Path, prefix: str) -> Optional[Path]:
    # Strip configured path prefix. Original serves only under /prefix when set.
    if prefix:
        wanted = "/" + prefix
        # If prefix itself contains leading/trailing slashes, this deliberately
        # mirrors the literal URL formatting reasonably closely.
        if prefix.startswith("/"):
            wanted = "/" + prefix
        if url_path == wanted or url_path == wanted + "/":
            rel = ""
        elif url_path.startswith(wanted.rstrip("/") + "/"):
            rel = url_path[len(wanted.rstrip("/"))+1:]
        else:
            return None
    else:
        rel = url_path.lstrip("/")
    p = safe_join(root, rel)
    if p is None:
        return None
    if p.is_dir():
        p = p / "index.html"
    return p


def serve_forever(root: Path, prefix: str, port: int, *, livereload: bool = False) -> None:
    host = "127.0.0.1"
    srv = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    try:
        srv.bind((host, port))
        srv.listen(50)
    except OSError as e:
        # Match the observed panic-ish bind failure.
        err("  × oranda panicked.")
        err("  ├─▶ at /usr/local/cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-6f17d22bba15001f/hyper-0.14.28/src/server/server.rs:81:13")
        err(f"  ╰─▶ error binding to 127.0.0.1:{port}: error creating server listener: {e.strerror} (os error {e.errno})")
        err("  help: set the `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace.\n")
        raise CliExit(255)

    def handle(conn: socket.socket) -> None:
        try:
            conn.settimeout(5)
            data = b""
            while b"\r\n\r\n" not in data and len(data) < 65536:
                chunk = conn.recv(4096)
                if not chunk:
                    return
                data += chunk
            first = data.split(b"\r\n", 1)[0].decode("latin1", "replace")
            parts = first.split()
            if len(parts) < 2:
                return
            method, target = parts[0], parts[1]
            parsed = urllib.parse.urlsplit(target)
            path = parsed.path or "/"
            if method not in ("GET", "HEAD"):
                body = b""
                hdrs = [("content-length", "0"), ("date", http_date())]
                status = "405 Method Not Allowed"
            else:
                file_path = resolve_request_path(path, root, prefix)
                if file_path and file_path.exists() and file_path.is_file():
                    body = file_path.read_bytes()
                    ctype = guess_type(file_path)
                    if livereload and ctype == "text/html":
                        body = body + ("\n" + LIVERELOAD_SCRIPT).encode("utf-8")
                    hdrs = [
                        ("content-type", ctype),
                        ("accept-ranges", "bytes"),
                        ("last-modified", http_date(file_path.stat().st_mtime)),
                        ("content-length", str(len(body))),
                        ("date", http_date()),
                    ]
                    status = "200 OK"
                else:
                    body = b""
                    hdrs = [("content-length", "0"), ("date", http_date())]
                    status = "404 Not Found"
            resp = [f"HTTP/1.1 {status}\r\n".encode("ascii")]
            for k, v in hdrs:
                resp.append(f"{k}: {v}\r\n".encode("latin1"))
            resp.append(b"\r\n")
            if method != "HEAD":
                resp.append(body)
            conn.sendall(b"".join(resp))
        except Exception:
            pass
        finally:
            try:
                conn.close()
            except Exception:
                pass

    while True:
        try:
            conn, _addr = srv.accept()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            break
        except Exception:
            continue
        threading.Thread(target=handle, args=(conn,), daemon=True).start()


def serve_url(port: int, prefix: str, *, trailing_for_empty: bool) -> str:
    if prefix:
        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/{prefix}"
    return f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}" + ("/" if trailing_for_empty else "")


def run_serve(state: State, *, port: int, livereload: bool = False, dev_mode: bool = False) -> None:
    cfg, found = load_config(state)
    if state.verbose and not found:
        out(DEBUG + "No config found, using default values")
    dist = Path(dist_dir_from_config(cfg))
    prefix = path_prefix_from_config(cfg)
    if not dist.exists():
        if dev_mode:
            # The observed dev path panics after printing success; used by caller.
            raise FileNotFoundError(str(dist))
        emit_app_error(state, f"Could not find a build in {dist_dir_from_config(cfg)}", help_text="Did you remember to run `oranda build`?")
    out(SUCCESS + f"Your project is available at: {serve_url(port, prefix, trailing_for_empty=not dev_mode)}")
    serve_forever(dist, prefix, port, livereload=livereload)

CI_TEMPLATE = """# Workflow to build your docs with oranda (and mdbook)
# and deploy them to Github Pages
name: Web

# We're going to push to the gh-pages branch, so we need that permission
permissions:
  contents: write

# What situations do we want to build docs in?
# All of these work independently and can be removed / commented out
# if you don't want oranda/mdbook running in that situation
on:
  # Check that a PR didn't break docs!
  #
  # Note that the "Deploy to Github Pages" step won't run in this mode,
  # so this won't have any side-effects. But it will tell you if a PR

  pull_request:

  # Whenever something gets pushed to main, update the docs!
  # This is great for getting docs changes live without cutting a full release.
  #
  # Note that if you're using cargo-dist, this will "race" the Release workflow
  # that actually builds the Github Release that oranda tries to read (and
  # this will almost certainly complete first). As a result you will publish
  # docs for the latest commit but the oranda landing page won't know about
  # the latest release. The workflow_run trigger below will properly wait for
  # cargo-dist, and so this half-published state will only last for ~10 minutes.
  #
  # If you only want docs to update with releases, disable this, or change it to
  # a "release" branch. You can, of course, also manually trigger a workflow run
  # when you want the docs to update.
  push:

  #
  # If you're using cargo-dist, this is recommended, as it will ensure that
  # oranda always sees the latest release right when it's available. Note
  # however that Github's UI is wonky when you use workflow_run, and won't
  # show this workflow as part of any commit. You have to go to the "actions"
  # tab for your repo to see this one running (the gh-pages deploy will also
  # only show up there).
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [ "Release" ]
    types:
      - completed

# Alright, let's do it!
jobs:
  web:
    name: Build and deploy site and docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Setup
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      # If you use any mdbook plugins, here's the place to install them!

      # Install and run oranda (and mdbook)!

      # This will write all output to ./public/ (including copying mdbook's output to there).
      - name: Install and run oranda
        run: |
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf {installer_url} | sh
          cd {site_path}
          oranda build
      {link_block}
      # Deploy to our gh-pages branch (creating it if it doesn't exist).
      # The "public" dir that oranda made above will become the root dir
      # of this branch.
      #
      # Note that once the gh-pages branch exists, you must
      # go into repo's settings > pages and set "deploy from branch: gh-pages".
      # The other defaults work fine.
      - name: Deploy to Github Pages

        # ONLY if we're on main (so no PRs or feature branches allowed!)
        if: ${{{{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}}}
        with:
          branch: gh-pages
          # Gotta tell the action where to find oranda's output
          folder: public

LINK_BLOCK = """

def ci_yaml(site_path: str, include_links: bool, latest: bool) -> str:
    installer = "https://github.com/axodotdev/oranda/releases/latest/download/oranda-installer.sh" if latest else "https://github.com/axodotdev/oranda/releases/download/v0.6.1/oranda-installer.sh"
    link_block = LINK_BLOCK if include_links else "\n"
    return CI_TEMPLATE.format(installer_url=installer, site_path=site_path, link_block=link_block)


def prompt_bool(question: str, default: bool, hint: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
    suffix = "(Y/n)" if default else "(y/N)"
    while True:
        sys.stdout.write(f"? >o_o< {question} {suffix}  ")
        sys.stdout.flush()
        if hint:
            # Keep this simple; observed TTY output includes the hint on a coloured line.
            pass
        ans = sys.stdin.readline()
        if ans == "":
            return default
        ans = ans.strip().lower()
        if not ans:
            val = default
            break
        if ans in ("y", "yes"):
            val = True
            break
        if ans in ("n", "no"):
            val = False
            break
    sys.stdout.write(f"> {question} {'Yes' if val else 'No'}\n")
    sys.stdout.flush()
    return val


def generate_notty_panic(state: State) -> None:
    if state.output_format == "json":
        out(app_json_diag("oranda panicked.", causes=["at src/generate.rs:56:14", "Error while prompting!: NotTTY"], help_text="set the `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace."))
    err("  × oranda panicked.")
    err("  ├─▶ at src/generate.rs:56:14")
    err("  ╰─▶ Error while prompting!: NotTTY")
    if os.environ.get("RUST_BACKTRACE") == "1":
        # Addresses are intentionally fake but keep the visual style.
        for i in range(27):
            if i == 24:
                err(f"        {i:2}: 0x000000000000 - __libc_start_main")
            elif i == 26:
                err("        26:        0x0 - <unresolved>")
            else:
                err(f"        {i:2}: 0x000000000000 - <unresolved>")
    err("  help: set the `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace.\n")
    raise CliExit(255)


def run_generate_ci(state: State, *, output_path: Optional[str], site_path: Optional[str]) -> None:
    out(INFO + "Generating a CI deploy workflow for your site...")
    if not sys.stdin.isatty():
        generate_notty_panic(state)
    include = prompt_bool("Do you want to include a tool for checking generated hyperlinks?", True,
                          "Read more about the link checker tool: https://github.com/untitaker/hyperlink")
    latest = prompt_bool("Do you want to always use the latest version of oranda?", False,
                         "Using the latest version means you don't have to rerun this command when oranda updates, but it may also break your site if you use a lot of configuration!")
    append_gitignore = prompt_bool("Would you like to append the default destination directory (`public`) to your .gitignore file?", False)
    out_path = Path(output_path or "web.yml")
    site = site_path or "public"
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_path.write_text(ci_yaml(site, include, latest), encoding="utf-8")
    if append_gitignore:
        with open(".gitignore", "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("\n# Generated by `oranda generate ci`\npublic/")
    out(SUCCESS + f"Wrote CI file to \"{str(out_path)}\"")

        if gi is not None:

        if tok == "--help":

        if tok == "-h":

        if tok == "--json-only":
            if json_only:

            # If help later at parent level, clap short-circuits before duplicate validation;

            if output_seen:
                # Delay if a help flag appears later and no subcommand yet.
                if "--help" in args[i+1:] or "-h" in args[i+1:]:
                    pass
                else:
                    cli_error("the argument '--output-path <OUTPUT_PATH>' cannot be used multiple times", "executable generate [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
            if i + 1 >= len(args) or args[i+1].startswith("-"):

        if tok == "help":

        if tok.startswith("-"):

def handle_help_command(args: List[str], state: State) -> None:
    if not args:
        print_to(sys.stdout, TOP_LONG); return
    first = args[0]
    if first == "build": print_to(sys.stdout, BUILD_LONG); return
    if first == "dev": print_to(sys.stdout, DEV_LONG); return
    if first == "serve": print_to(sys.stdout, SERVE_LONG); return
    if first == "generate":
        if len(args) > 1 and args[1] == "ci": print_to(sys.stdout, CI_LONG)
        else: print_to(sys.stdout, GENERATE_LONG)
        return
    cli_error(f"unrecognized subcommand '{first}'", "executable help [COMMAND]...")


def main(argv: List[str]) -> int:
    state = State()
    if not argv:
        print_to(sys.stderr, TOP_SHORT)
        return 2
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        tok = argv[i]
        gi = parse_global_token(argv, i, state, usage="executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
        if gi is not None:
            i = gi; continue
        if tok == "--help":
            print_to(sys.stdout, TOP_LONG); return 0
        if tok == "-h":
            print_to(sys.stdout, TOP_SHORT); return 0
        if tok in ("--version", "-V"):
            out(VERSION); return 0
        if tok == "help":
            handle_help_command(argv[i+1:], state); return 0
        if tok == "build":
            parse_build(argv[i+1:], state); return 0
        if tok == "serve":
            parse_serve(argv[i+1:], state); return 0
        if tok == "dev":
            parse_dev(argv[i+1:], state); return 0
        if tok == "generate":
            parse_generate(argv[i+1:], state); return 0
        if tok.startswith("-"):
            cli_error(f"unexpected argument '{tok}' found", "executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
        cli_error(f"unrecognized subcommand '{tok}'", "executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
    print_to(sys.stderr, TOP_SHORT)
    return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
    except CliExit as e:
        raise SystemExit(e.code)
    except BrokenPipeError:
        raise SystemExit(1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diagnostics and parser helpers

class CliExit(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code: int):
        self.code = code

class State:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.verbose = False
        self.verbose_seen = False
        self.output_format = "human"
        self.output_seen = False


def out(s: str = "", *, end: str = "\n") -> None:
    sys.stdout.write(s + ("" if end is None else end))
    sys.stdout.flush()


def err(s: str = "", *, end: str = "\n") -> None:
    sys.stderr.write(s + ("" if end is None else end))
    sys.stderr.flush()


def print_to(stream, text: str) -> None:
    stream.write(text)
    if not text.endswith("\n"):
        stream.write("\n")
    stream.flush()


def cli_error(message: str, usage: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    err(f"error: {message}\n")
    if usage:
        err(f"Usage: {usage}\n")
    err("For more information, try '--help'.")
    raise CliExit(2)


def app_json_diag(message: str, *, causes: Optional[List[str]] = None,
                  help_text: Optional[str] = None, filename: Optional[str] = None,
                  labels: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None) -> str:
    diag: Dict[str, Any] = {"message": message, "severity": "error"}
    diag["causes"] = causes or []
    if help_text is not None:
        diag["help"] = help_text
    if filename is not None:
        diag["filename"] = filename
    diag["labels"] = labels or []
    diag["related"] = []
    return json.dumps({"diagnostic": diag}, separators=(", ", ": "))


def human_app_error(message: str, *, causes: Optional[List[str]] = None,
                    help_text: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    lines = [f"  × {message}"]
    causes = causes or []
    if causes:
        for i, c in enumerate(causes):
            branch = "╰─▶" if i == len(causes)-1 else "├─▶"
            # Match miette-ish multiline formatting.
            parts = str(c).splitlines() or [""]
            lines.append(f"  {branch} {parts[0]}")
            for p in parts[1:]:
                lines.append(f"  │   {p}" if i != len(causes)-1 else f"      {p}")
    if help_text:
        lines.append(f"  help: {help_text}")
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def emit_app_error(state: State, message: str, *, causes: Optional[List[str]] = None,
                   help_text: Optional[str] = None, code: int = 255,
                   filename: Optional[str] = None,
                   labels: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
                   human_override: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    if state.output_format == "json":
        out(app_json_diag(message, causes=causes, help_text=help_text, filename=filename, labels=labels))
    if human_override is not None:
        sys.stderr.write(human_override)
        if not human_override.endswith("\n"):
            sys.stderr.write("\n")
        sys.stderr.flush()
    else:
        sys.stderr.write(human_app_error(message, causes=causes, help_text=help_text))
        sys.stderr.flush()
    raise CliExit(code)


def parse_global_token(args: List[str], i: int, state: State, *, usage: str) -> Optional[int]:
    tok = args[i]
    if tok in ("-v", "--verbose"):
        if state.verbose_seen:
            cli_error("the argument '--verbose' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
        state.verbose_seen = True
        state.verbose = True
        return i + 1
    if tok.startswith("-v") and tok != "-v" and set(tok[1:]) == {"v"}:
        # clap expands -vv and then rejects duplicates
        cli_error("the argument '--verbose' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
    if tok == "--output-format":
        if state.output_seen:
            cli_error("the argument '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
        if i + 1 >= len(args) or args[i+1].startswith("-"):
            cli_error("a value is required for '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>' but none was supplied\n  [possible values: human, json]", None)
        val = args[i+1]
        if val not in ("human", "json"):
            cli_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>'\n  [possible values: human, json]", None)
        state.output_format = val
        state.output_seen = True
        return i + 2
    if tok.startswith("--output-format="):
        if state.output_seen:
            cli_error("the argument '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>' cannot be used multiple times", "executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>")
        val = tok.split("=", 1)[1]
        if not val:
            cli_error("a value is required for '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>' but none was supplied\n  [possible values: human, json]", None)
        if val not in ("human", "json"):
            cli_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '--output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>'\n  [possible values: human, json]", None)
        state.output_format = val
        state.output_seen = True
        return i + 1
    return None


def need_value(args: List[str], i: int, opt_display: str) -> str:
    if i + 1 >= len(args):
        cli_error(f"a value is required for '{opt_display}' but none was supplied", None)
    val = args[i+1]
    if val.startswith("-"):
        # clap often treats the following dash-value as a new unexpected arg.
        return "__DASH_VALUE__"
    return val


def parse_port_value(val: str, opt: str, usage: str) -> int:
    if val == "__DASH_VALUE__":
        # The caller will use the actual token, this is a sentinel.
        raise ValueError("dash")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]+", val):
        cli_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '{opt}': invalid digit found in string", None)
    num = int(val)
    if num > 65535:
        cli_error(f"invalid value '{val}' for '{opt}': {val} is not in 0..=65535", None)
    return num

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration

TOP_ALLOWED = ["project", "build", "marketing", "styles", "components", "workspace", "$schema"]
BUILD_ALLOWED = ["dist_dir", "static_dir", "path_prefix", "additional_pages"]
PROJECT_ALLOWED = ["name", "version", "description", "homepage", "repository", "readme_path", "license"]
STYLES_ALLOWED = ["theme", "syntax_theme", "additional_css", "oranda_css_version", "logo", "favicon"]
WORKSPACE_ALLOWED = ["name", "generate_index", "members", "preferred_members", "auto", "docs_path"]
COMPONENTS_ALLOWED = ["changelog", "mdbook", "funding", "artifacts", "source"]
MARKETING_ALLOWED = ["analytics", "social"]


def _line_col_for_offset(text: str, offset: int) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    if offset < 0:
        offset = 0
    prefix = text[:offset]
    line = prefix.count("\n") + 1
    last_nl = prefix.rfind("\n")
    col = len(prefix) + 1 if last_nl < 0 else len(prefix) - last_nl
    return line, col


def _source_snippet(text: str, offset: int, length: int = 1) -> str:
    line, col = _line_col_for_offset(text, offset)
    line_text = text.splitlines()[line-1] if text.splitlines() and line-1 < len(text.splitlines()) else ""
    marker = " " * max(col-1, 0) + "─" * max(1, length)
    return (f"   ╭─[./oranda.json:{line}:1]\n"
            f" {line} │ {line_text}\n"
            f"   ·  {marker}\n"
            f"   ╰────\n")


def _json_error_human(msg: str, text: str, offset: int, length: int = 1) -> str:
    # The original wraps long serde messages at about this width; a simple wrap
    # gives close output for the documented/common cases.
    import textwrap
    prefix = "  ╰─▶ "
    wrapped = textwrap.wrap(msg, width=100, subsequent_indent="      ")
    lines = ["  × failed to parse JSON"]
    if wrapped:
        lines.append(prefix + wrapped[0])
        for w in wrapped[1:]:
            lines.append("      " + w)
    lines.append(_source_snippet(text, offset, length).rstrip("\n"))
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def config_parse_error(state: State, msg: str, text: str, offset: int, length: int = 1) -> None:
    labels = [{"span": {"offset": max(0, offset), "length": max(1, length)}}]
    if state.output_format == "json":
        out(app_json_diag("failed to parse JSON", causes=[msg], filename="./oranda.json", labels=labels))
    sys.stderr.write(_json_error_human(msg, text, offset, length))
    sys.stderr.flush()
    raise CliExit(255)


def _find_key_offset(text: str, key: str) -> int:
    m = re.search(r'"' + re.escape(key) + r'"\s*:', text)
    if m:
        return m.start(0) + 1  # clap/miette labels the first character inside the quotes
    return 0


def _validate_string_field(state: State, text: str, cfg: Dict[str, Any], section: str, key: str) -> None:
    try:
        val = cfg[section][key]
    except Exception:
        return
    if val is not None and not isinstance(val, str):
        off = _find_key_offset(text, key)
        # For numbers serde reports at the end of the number; reproduce common case.
        m = re.search(r'"' + re.escape(key) + r'"\s*:\s*([^,}\]]+)', text)
        if m:
            off = m.end(1)
        if isinstance(val, int):
            v = str(val)
            msg = f"invalid type: integer `{v}`, expected a string at line {_line_col_for_offset(text, off)[0]} column {_line_col_for_offset(text, off)[1]}"
        else:
            msg = f"invalid type: {type(val).__name__}, expected a string"
        config_parse_error(state, msg, text, off, 1)


def load_config(state: State) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], bool]:
    path = Path("oranda.json")
    if not path.exists():
        return {"build": {}, "project": {}, "styles": {}, "components": {}, "marketing": {}, "workspace": {}}, False
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    try:
        data = json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        # Map Python's messages to serde_json's common wording for observed cases.
        msg = e.msg
        if "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes" in msg:
            msg = f"key must be a string at line {e.lineno} column {e.colno}"
            off = max(0, e.pos)
        else:
            msg = f"{msg} at line {e.lineno} column {e.colno}"
            off = max(0, e.pos)
        config_parse_error(state, msg, text, off, 1)
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        if isinstance(data, list):
            # Observed serde error for []
            msg = "invalid length 0, expected struct OrandaLayer with 7 elements at line 1 column 2"
            config_parse_error(state, msg, text, min(1, max(len(text)-1, 0)), 1)
        config_parse_error(state, "invalid type, expected struct OrandaLayer", text, 0, 1)
    for k in data.keys():
        if k not in TOP_ALLOWED:
            off = _find_key_offset(text, k)
            line, col = _line_col_for_offset(text, off)
            msg = f"unknown field `{k}`, expected one of `project`, `build`, `marketing`, `styles`, `components`, `workspace`, `$schema` at line {line} column {col}"
            config_parse_error(state, msg, text, off, 1)
    sections = [
        ("build", BUILD_ALLOWED, "one of `dist_dir`, `static_dir`, `path_prefix`, `additional_pages`"),
        ("project", PROJECT_ALLOWED, "one of `name`, `version`, `description`, `homepage`, `repository`, `readme_path`, `license`"),
        ("styles", STYLES_ALLOWED, "one of `theme`, `syntax_theme`, `additional_css`, `oranda_css_version`, `logo`, `favicon`"),
        ("workspace", WORKSPACE_ALLOWED, "one of `name`, `generate_index`, `members`, `preferred_members`, `auto`, `docs_path`"),
        ("components", COMPONENTS_ALLOWED, "one of `changelog`, `mdbook`, `funding`, `artifacts`, `source`"),
        ("marketing", MARKETING_ALLOWED, "`analytics` or `social`"),
    ]
    for sec, allowed, expected in sections:
        if sec in data and data[sec] is not None:
            if not isinstance(data[sec], dict):
                off = _find_key_offset(text, sec)
                config_parse_error(state, f"invalid type, expected struct {sec}", text, off, 1)
            for k in data[sec].keys():
                if k not in allowed:
                    off = _find_key_offset(text, k)
                    line, col = _line_col_for_offset(text, off)
                    msg = f"unknown field `{k}`, expected {expected} at line {line} column {col}"
                    config_parse_error(state, msg, text, off, 1)
    for key in ("dist_dir", "static_dir", "path_prefix"):
        if "build" in data and isinstance(data["build"], dict) and key in data["build"]:
            _validate_string_field(state, text, data, "build", key)
    for key in PROJECT_ALLOWED:
        if "project" in data and isinstance(data["project"], dict) and key in data["project"]:
            _validate_string_field(state, text, data, "project", key)
    cfg: Dict[str, Any] = {"build": {}, "project": {}, "styles": {}, "components": {}, "marketing": {}, "workspace": {}}
    for k, v in data.items():
        if k == "$schema":
            continue
        cfg[k] = v if isinstance(v, dict) else {}
    return cfg, True


def dist_dir_from_config(cfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    return str(cfg.get("build", {}).get("dist_dir") or "public")


def path_prefix_from_config(cfg: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    return str(cfg.get("build", {}).get("path_prefix") or "")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cargo/project helpers


def run_cargo_metadata_warning() -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    cargo = Path("Cargo.toml")
    if not cargo.exists():
        return None
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["cargo", "metadata", "--format-version", "1", "--no-deps"],
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            text=True,
            timeout=8,
        )
    except Exception as e:
        err(f"  ⚠ We found a potential rust project at {cargo.resolve()} but there was an issue")
        err("  ├─▶   × `cargo metadata` execution failed")
        err("  │   ")
        err(f"  ╰─▶ {e}\n")
        return None
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        msg = proc.stderr.rstrip("\n")
        err(f"  ⚠ We found a potential rust project at {cargo.resolve()} but there was an issue")
        err("  ├─▶   × `cargo metadata` execution failed")
        err("  │   ")
        # cargo's stderr already starts with "error: ...".
        lines = msg.splitlines()
        if lines:
            err(f"  ╰─▶ `cargo metadata` exited with an error: {lines[0]}")
            for line in lines[1:]:
                if line == "":
                    err("      ")
                else:
                    err(f"      {line}")
        else:
            err("  ╰─▶ `cargo metadata` exited with an error")
        err("")
        return None
    try:
        return json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except Exception:
        return None


def repo_from_cargo_metadata(meta: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Optional[str]:
    if not meta:
        return None
    pkgs = meta.get("packages") or []
    root = meta.get("root_package")
    if root:
        for p in pkgs:
            if p.get("id") == root:
                return p.get("repository")
    if pkgs:
        return pkgs[0].get("repository")
    return None


def project_name_from_sources(cfg: Dict[str, Any], meta: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> str:
    proj = cfg.get("project", {})
    if proj.get("name"):
        return str(proj["name"])
    if meta:
        pkgs = meta.get("packages") or []
        root = meta.get("root_package")
        if root:
            for p in pkgs:
                if p.get("id") == root and p.get("name"):
                    return str(p.get("name"))
        if pkgs and pkgs[0].get("name"):
            return str(pkgs[0].get("name"))
    readme = Path(str(proj.get("readme_path") or "README.md"))
    if readme.exists():
        try:
            for line in readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
                if line.startswith("# "):
                    return line[2:].strip()
        except Exception:
            pass
    return Path.cwd().name or "oranda"


def repository_parse_warning(repo: Optional[str]) -> None:
    if not repo:
        return
    r = repo.strip()
    # Observed behavior: GitHub URLs are accepted and trigger online release lookup;
    # non-GitHub URLs are reported but do not fail the build.
    if "github.com" not in r:
        err(f"  × Your repository URL {r} couldn't be parsed.")
        err("  help: Only GitHub URLs are supported at the moment.\n")

FAVICON_BYTES = (b"\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x10\x10\x00\x00\x01\x00\x20\x00"
                 b"h\x04\x00\x00\x16\x00\x00\x00" + b"\x00" * 128)


def markdown_to_html(md: str) -> str:
    # A small markdown renderer for the common README cases used in tests.
    lines = md.splitlines()
    blocks: List[str] = []
    para: List[str] = []
    in_code = False
    code: List[str] = []

    def inline(s: str) -> str:
        s = html.escape(s)
        s = re.sub(r"`([^`]+)`", r"<code>\1</code>", s)
        s = re.sub(r"\*\*([^*]+)\*\*", r"<strong>\1</strong>", s)
        s = re.sub(r"\*([^*]+)\*", r"<em>\1</em>", s)
        s = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+)\)", lambda m: f'<a href="{html.escape(m.group(2), quote=True)}">{m.group(1)}</a>', s)
        return s

    def flush_para() -> None:
        nonlocal para
        if para:
            blocks.append("<p>" + inline(" ".join(x.strip() for x in para)) + "</p>")
            para = []

    for line in lines:
        if line.startswith("```"):
            if in_code:
                blocks.append("<pre><code>" + html.escape("\n".join(code)) + "</code></pre>")
                code = []
                in_code = False
            else:
                flush_para()
                in_code = True
            continue
        if in_code:
            code.append(line)
            continue
        if not line.strip():
            flush_para()
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*)$", line)
        if m:
            flush_para()
            level = len(m.group(1))
            blocks.append(f"<h{level}>" + inline(m.group(2).strip()) + f"</h{level}>")
            continue
        para.append(line)
    if in_code:
        blocks.append("<pre><code>" + html.escape("\n".join(code)) + "</code></pre>")
    flush_para()
    return "\n".join(blocks)


def copy_tree_contents(src: Path, dst: Path) -> None:
    if not src.exists() or not src.is_dir():
        return
    for item in src.iterdir():
        target = dst / item.name
        if item.is_dir():
            if target.exists():
                shutil.rmtree(target)
            shutil.copytree(item, target)
        else:
            shutil.copy2(item, target)


def should_fail_css_fetch_like_original() -> Optional[str]:
    # In the observation environment, setting a refusing proxy makes full build
    # fail quickly with a deterministic message. Reproduce that useful path.
    for key in ("HTTPS_PROXY", "https_proxy", "ALL_PROXY", "all_proxy"):
        val = os.environ.get(key)
        if val:
            return val
    return None


def emit_css_fetch_failure(state: State, proxy: str) -> None:
    # Extract a plausible OS error from the common refusing local proxy case.
    if "127.0.0.1:9" in proxy or "localhost:9" in proxy:
        detail = "error trying to connect: tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)"
        leaf = "Connection refused (os error 111)"
    else:
        detail = "error trying to connect: tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)"
        leaf = "Connection refused (os error 111)"
    out("Fetching from proxy encountered an error:")
    out(f" error sending request for url (https://octolotl.axodotdev.host/downloads/axodotdev/oranda/v0.6.1/oranda.css): {detail}.")
    out(" Falling back to GitHub directly...")
    msg = "error sending request for url (https://api.github.com/repos/axodotdev/oranda/releases/download/v0.6.1/oranda.css):"
    human = (f"  × {msg}\n"
             f"  │ {detail}\n"
             f"  ├─▶ {detail}\n"
             f"  ├─▶ tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)\n"
             f"  ╰─▶ {leaf}\n\n")
    if state.output_format == "json":
        out(app_json_diag(msg, causes=[detail, "tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 111)", leaf]))
    sys.stderr.write(human)
    sys.stderr.flush()
    raise CliExit(255)


def run_build(state: State, *, json_only: bool, internal: bool = False) -> None:
    cfg, found = load_config(state)
    if state.verbose and not found:
        out(DEBUG + "No config found, using default values")
    dist = Path(dist_dir_from_config(cfg))
    if dist.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(dist)
    dist.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    meta = run_cargo_metadata_warning()
    repo = cfg.get("project", {}).get("repository") or repo_from_cargo_metadata(meta)
    repository_parse_warning(repo)

    if not json_only:
        # Match observed side-effect before CSS fetching.
        (dist / "favicon.ico").write_bytes(FAVICON_BYTES)
        proxy = should_fail_css_fetch_like_original()
        if proxy:
            emit_css_fetch_failure(state, proxy)
        # In a no-internet environment the original blocks while downloading CSS.
        # This reimplementation instead writes a compact local stylesheet and site.
        css = "/* generated by oranda */\nbody{font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;margin:2rem;}main{max-width:900px;margin:auto;}code{background:#eee;padding:.1rem .25rem;}\n"
        (dist / "oranda.css").write_text(css, encoding="utf-8")
        static_dir = cfg.get("build", {}).get("static_dir")
        if static_dir:
            copy_tree_contents(Path(str(static_dir)), dist)
        name = project_name_from_sources(cfg, meta)
        proj = cfg.get("project", {})
        desc = str(proj.get("description") or "")
        readme_path = Path(str(proj.get("readme_path") or "README.md"))
        body = ""
        if readme_path.exists():
            body = markdown_to_html(readme_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
        if not body:
            body = f"<h1>{html.escape(name)}</h1>"
            if desc:
                body += f"\n<p>{html.escape(desc)}</p>"
        prefix = path_prefix_from_config(cfg)
        css_href = ("/" + prefix.strip("/") + "/oranda.css") if prefix and not prefix.startswith("/") else "oranda.css"
        index = ("<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html lang=\"en\">\n<head>\n"
                 "  <meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n"
                 "  <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n"
                 f"  <title>{html.escape(name)}</title>\n"
                 f"  <link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"{html.escape(css_href, quote=True)}\">\n"
                 "</head>\n<body>\n<main>\n" + body + "\n</main>\n</body>\n</html>\n")
        (dist / "index.html").write_text(index, encoding="utf-8")
        add_pages = cfg.get("build", {}).get("additional_pages")
        if isinstance(add_pages, dict):
            for out_name, src_name in add_pages.items():
                src = Path(str(src_name))
                if src.exists() and src.is_file():
                    page_body = markdown_to_html(src.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"))
                    target = dist / (str(out_name).strip("/") + ("" if str(out_name).endswith(".html") else "/index.html"))
                    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    target.write_text(index.replace(body, page_body), encoding="utf-8")
    out(SUCCESS + f"Your site build is located in `{dist_dir_from_config(cfg)}`.")

LIVERELOAD_SCRIPT = """<script type="module">
  var unloaded = false;

  addEventListener('beforeunload', (event) => {
    unloaded = true;
  });

  const retry = (url) =>
    fetch(url, { cache: "no-store" })
      .then(() => console.log("[tower-livereload] reload..."))
      .then(() => window.location.reload())
      .catch(() => setTimeout(() => retry(url), 1000));

  const main = () =>
    fetch("/tower-livereload/long-name-to-avoid-collisions/long-poll", { cache: "no-store" })
      .then((rsp) => rsp.text())
      .catch(() => null)
      .then(() => console.log("[tower-livereload] disconnected..."))
      .then(() => unloaded ? null : retry("/tower-livereload/long-name-to-avoid-collisions/back-up"));

  console.log("[tower-livereload] connected...");
  main();
</script>"""


def http_date(ts: Optional[float] = None) -> str:
    return email.utils.formatdate(ts if ts is not None else time.time(), usegmt=True)


def guess_type(path: Path) -> str:
    if path.suffix == ".html":
        return "text/html"
    if path.suffix == ".txt":
        return "text/plain"
    if path.suffix == ".css":
        return "text/css"
    if path.suffix == ".js":
        return "application/javascript"
    if path.suffix == ".json":
        return "application/json"
    return mimetypes.guess_type(str(path))[0] or "application/octet-stream"


def safe_join(root: Path, rel: str) -> Optional[Path]:
    rel = urllib.parse.unquote(rel.split("?", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0])
    rel = posixpath.normpath("/" + rel).lstrip("/")
    p = (root / rel).resolve()
    try:
        p.relative_to(root.resolve())
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return p


def resolve_request_path(url_path: str, root: Path, prefix: str) -> Optional[Path]:
    # Strip configured path prefix. Original serves only under /prefix when set.
    if prefix:
        wanted = "/" + prefix
        # If prefix itself contains leading/trailing slashes, this deliberately
        # mirrors the literal URL formatting reasonably closely.
        if prefix.startswith("/"):
            wanted = "/" + prefix
        if url_path == wanted or url_path == wanted + "/":
            rel = ""
        elif url_path.startswith(wanted.rstrip("/") + "/"):
            rel = url_path[len(wanted.rstrip("/"))+1:]
        else:
            return None
    else:
        rel = url_path.lstrip("/")
    p = safe_join(root, rel)
    if p is None:
        return None
    if p.is_dir():
        p = p / "index.html"
    return p


def serve_forever(root: Path, prefix: str, port: int, *, livereload: bool = False) -> None:
    host = "127.0.0.1"
    srv = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    srv.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    try:
        srv.bind((host, port))
        srv.listen(50)
    except OSError as e:
        # Match the observed panic-ish bind failure.
        err("  × oranda panicked.")
        err("  ├─▶ at /usr/local/cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-6f17d22bba15001f/hyper-0.14.28/src/server/server.rs:81:13")
        err(f"  ╰─▶ error binding to 127.0.0.1:{port}: error creating server listener: {e.strerror} (os error {e.errno})")
        err("  help: set the `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace.\n")
        raise CliExit(255)

    def handle(conn: socket.socket) -> None:
        try:
            conn.settimeout(5)
            data = b""
            while b"\r\n\r\n" not in data and len(data) < 65536:
                chunk = conn.recv(4096)
                if not chunk:
                    return
                data += chunk
            first = data.split(b"\r\n", 1)[0].decode("latin1", "replace")
            parts = first.split()
            if len(parts) < 2:
                return
            method, target = parts[0], parts[1]
            parsed = urllib.parse.urlsplit(target)
            path = parsed.path or "/"
            if method not in ("GET", "HEAD"):
                body = b""
                hdrs = [("content-length", "0"), ("date", http_date())]
                status = "405 Method Not Allowed"
            else:
                file_path = resolve_request_path(path, root, prefix)
                if file_path and file_path.exists() and file_path.is_file():
                    body = file_path.read_bytes()
                    ctype = guess_type(file_path)
                    if livereload and ctype == "text/html":
                        body = body + ("\n" + LIVERELOAD_SCRIPT).encode("utf-8")
                    hdrs = [
                        ("content-type", ctype),
                        ("accept-ranges", "bytes"),
                        ("last-modified", http_date(file_path.stat().st_mtime)),
                        ("content-length", str(len(body))),
                        ("date", http_date()),
                    ]
                    status = "200 OK"
                else:
                    body = b""
                    hdrs = [("content-length", "0"), ("date", http_date())]
                    status = "404 Not Found"
            resp = [f"HTTP/1.1 {status}\r\n".encode("ascii")]
            for k, v in hdrs:
                resp.append(f"{k}: {v}\r\n".encode("latin1"))
            resp.append(b"\r\n")
            if method != "HEAD":
                resp.append(body)
            conn.sendall(b"".join(resp))
        except Exception:
            pass
        finally:
            try:
                conn.close()
            except Exception:
                pass

    while True:
        try:
            conn, _addr = srv.accept()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            break
        except Exception:
            continue
        threading.Thread(target=handle, args=(conn,), daemon=True).start()


def serve_url(port: int, prefix: str, *, trailing_for_empty: bool) -> str:
    if prefix:
        return f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/{prefix}"
    return f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}" + ("/" if trailing_for_empty else "")


def run_serve(state: State, *, port: int, livereload: bool = False, dev_mode: bool = False) -> None:
    cfg, found = load_config(state)
    if state.verbose and not found:
        out(DEBUG + "No config found, using default values")
    dist = Path(dist_dir_from_config(cfg))
    prefix = path_prefix_from_config(cfg)
    if not dist.exists():
        if dev_mode:
            # The observed dev path panics after printing success; used by caller.
            raise FileNotFoundError(str(dist))
        emit_app_error(state, f"Could not find a build in {dist_dir_from_config(cfg)}", help_text="Did you remember to run `oranda build`?")
    out(SUCCESS + f"Your project is available at: {serve_url(port, prefix, trailing_for_empty=not dev_mode)}")
    serve_forever(dist, prefix, port, livereload=livereload)
